title: ExpertKnowledge 2.0: what the people running the process already know
description: Unpublished observations, prior internal experiments, operational constraints and expert judgement, recorded as structure rather than buried in a prompt. It is a first-class private evidence class: it may change which hypothesis is worth testing, narrow a parameter search range, and change how a result is interpreted. It may never become a literature citation, a measured dataset, or a verified causal relationship, and the distinction between 'I know this from experiments' and 'this is my hypothesis' is kept, because they are not the same evidence.

knowledge_type.description: prior_internal_experiment means data was collected. expert_judgement means it was not. Treating them the same would let an opinion carry the weight of an experiment.

scope.description: Where this applies. Knowledge about one cell line at one stage is not knowledge about the process.

parameter_claims.description: The structured part: a claim about a canonical parameter, which may narrow a search range or deprioritise a direction. Never a value to adopt.

consequence.description: What was observed to happen, in the user's words

citable.description: Expert knowledge is never a literature citation. A claim needs a source, a paragraph and a verbatim quote; a recollection has none.

may_set_protocol_value.description: It can change which parameter is investigated and over what range. It cannot supply the value, which stays a design choice until evidence supports it.
